subject: PX Health renewal: marketplace private-offer coordination & staggered acceptance
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@pixlhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal request & private offer for PixlHealth

Hi Sofia,

Quick note from procurement — our current Marketplace contract with Redwood is up for renewal around the end of the month. Wed like to pursue a private-offer in the AWS Marketplace for a 12-month term and increase committed capacity by ~40% compared to current run-rate. We also have an Azure presence and would like to keep a small reserved buffer there (15% of committed capacity) behind a secondary private-offer if that makes sense.

Can you share the paperwork and whether Redwood can accept a single PO that maps to two private-offer entries (AWS primary, Azure secondary) with staggered acceptance? Ideal outcomes for us:
- Single Purchase Order to finance (easier for our AP)
- Two private-offer entries so we can stagger activation dates across regions
- Ability to top up capacity mid-term (Q2) without a full amendment

I attached a draft PO that procurement started. Please loop in whoever handles marketplace private-offer logistics.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Cloud Ops, PixlHealth
elena@pixlhealth.com

Attachment: PXHealth_PO_draft_20261112.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@pixlhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T13:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request & private offer for PixlHealth

Thanks Elena — looping in Account and Marketplace (Marissa & Karthik) to coordinate the private-offer flow and acceptance windows. Quick answers up front: yes, we can accept a single PO and create two private-offer entries (AWS primary, Azure secondary) that map to the same commitment. We can also support a staggered acceptance so activation and billing are split across the two entries.

A few operational questions to confirm the right paperwork:
- Do you want the Azure private-offer to be a fixed reserve (15% of committed units) or a burstable buffer (pay for what you use beyond AWS)?
- For mid-term top-ups, is finance OK with a PO amendment or would you prefer a signed change order at the time of uplift?
- Preferred activation window for AWS (we can do immediate upon acceptance or schedule a 30-day lead to align procurement/finance).

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa will prepare a two-line private-offer draft (PDF) that we can share with your procurement — one line for AWS, one for Azure.
2) Well include a staggered acceptance clause and a simple change-order template for mid-term uplifts.
3) Quick sync (30m) — can we do Tuesday 11/16 at 9am PT?

Marissa/Karthik: please flag any marketplace constraints (billing tranches, invoice staging, or acceptance windows) we should bake into the draft.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
From: Elena Morales <elena@pixlhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean O'Neill <sean.oneill@pixlhealth.com>, procurement@pixlhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-13T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request & private offer for PixlHealth

Hi Sofia — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below: 
- Azure: wed prefer the Azure entry be a fixed reserve (15% of the committed units) to simplify forecasting.
- Mid-term top-ups: procurement prefers a PO amendment (single new PO or an addendum) that finance can process.
- Activation: AWS should be the immediate activation upon private-offer acceptance; Azure activation can be chained 60 days after AWS acceptance.

We can do the 11/16 sync you suggested — Sean (ccd) will join as our procurement contact. Ive also attached a version of the PO with our internal GL codes filled out.

Regards,
Elena

Attachment: PXHealth_PO_draft_20261113_with_codes.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@pixlhealth.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, legal.contracts@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood private-offer draft & invoice staging (PX-2026-011)

Elena, Sean — good to meet earlier. Per our sync, attached is Redwoods Private-Offer draft (Redwood_PrivateOffer_PXHealth_v2.pdf). Highlights:
- Two-line private offer: Line 1 = AWS (primary) 12-month term, committed units + 40% uplift.
- Line 2 = Azure (reserve) 12-month term, 15% reserved capacity; activation scheduled 60 days after AWS acceptance.
- Billing: single PO maps to both lines; we will stage invoices per acceptance window (AWS invoice at acceptance, Azure invoice upon activation).
- Mid-term top-ups: change-order template included. Finance prefers an executed amendment/PO when a top-up occurs — well make that process as lightweight as possible.

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_PXHealth_v2.pdf (private-offer draft), ChangeOrder_Template_PX.pdf
HubSpot Deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/12345

Action items:
- Elena/Sean: confirm GL codes and whether AP needs a consolidated invoice or separate line-item invoices for accounting.
- Legal: quick review of CLIN around acceptance windows and billing triggers (Legal, please comment inline by 11/17 EOD).

Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Signed PO & next steps (PX-2026-011)

Marissa / Sofia — attached is the signed PO (PXHealth_Signed_PO_20261118.pdf). AP confirms they can process a single PO and would prefer one consolidated invoice that references both private-offer line items; they will post the GL mapping to the invoice once it lands in their system.

Next steps from Redwood side that we need:
- Confirmation of invoice format and the billing contact for remittance.
- Expected activation date for AWS once Redwood accepts the private-offer (wed like the activation window to be within 3 business days of acceptance).
- Docusign flow for the private-offer (if legal signs on the PDF draft well expect a Docusign to finalize).

Thanks,
Elena
